string-array.name: help_bodies
string-array.item: Tap the page-plus button in the bottom-right corner to open a new untitled.txt tab. Your existing tabs stay open.
Hold the page-plus button in the bottom-right corner and choose New Markdown file (.md). A blank untitled.md tab opens in source editing mode, ready to write.
Tap Open and choose a .txt, .md, or .markdown file through Android’s file picker. It opens in its own tab and leaves your other tabs untouched.
Choose a supported text file in your Android file manager and open it with Hermes Text Editor.

Every document lives in its own tab under the title bar. The open tab is welded to the page beneath it by a curved foot, so you can tell at a glance which page you are editing. Tap a tab to switch, tap × on it to close. Drag a long tab name sideways to read the rest of it; the row scrolls sideways when the tabs no longer fit.
Your tabs, the active one and its scroll position come back when you return to the app, including after Android has closed it in the background. Unsaved text stays in the draft of that tab.

Recent is not a tab. Tap the app icon at the left of the strip and the list covers the document; while it is showing, the icon grows a little and takes a tinted plate, so you can tell you are not in a document. It lists the files this app has opened, newest first, with New and Open at the top. Tapping a file reopens it, or jumps to the tab that already holds it, and pressing and holding a closed file forgets it from the list. Closing the last tab lands here too, and so does a cold start with nothing to restore.
Tap to place the cursor, type, select, copy and paste. Long filenames stay on one line; swipe the name sideways to read it.
In Edit Markdown, headings, emphasis, links, lists, quotes and code are styled as you type. All Markdown symbols remain visible and editable; source text is preserved.

Use the three-dot menu to switch modes. Preview is formatted for reading; Edit Markdown shows the original source. Switching keeps approximately the same document section. Tap a web link in Preview to open your browser.
Tap the floppy Save button in the bottom-right corner to write the current file. A short message confirms success. If saving fails, your draft remains intact; use Save as… to make a copy.
Hold the floppy Save button in the bottom-right corner to open Save as… and Export as plain text….
Choose Save as… and select .txt or .md, then a filename and folder. The copy keeps the exact source content, including Markdown symbols.
Hold the floppy Save button and choose Export as plain text… for a readable .txt copy without Markdown formatting. The original Markdown file is unchanged.

Use the curved Undo and Redo buttons at the bottom-right corner. Rapid typing is grouped; unavailable actions are disabled. History is bounded and local. Undo and Redo do not change the saved file until Save.

Choose Find in the three-dot menu. Type a word or phrase and use the previous/next icons. The counter shows current / total matches. Find does not edit text. In Markdown Preview it switches to source mode. Close Find to restore the Undo/Redo control.
Pinch with two fingers to enlarge or reduce text. Zoom applies to editing and Preview, stays between comfortable limits and is saved locally. One finger still scrolls and selects normally.
Use the sun/moon item in the three-dot menu to switch themes. Document styling updates with the theme.
Choose English or فارسی in the three-dot menu. The interface language is saved locally; your document text is not translated.

Choose Left-to-right or Right-to-left in the three-dot menu. Clearly Persian or English files may receive a suggestion when their direction differs from the current setting. Manual direction remains your choice.

Hermes Text Editor works offline: no ads, analytics, tracking, WebView or Internet permission. Your draft is recovered locally. Files are accessed through Android’s picker or file-manager opening. Links open externally only when tapped.
